### GSE/symbolic/resolution.py
def _collapse_phrase_to_entity(phrase: Phrase) -> Expression:
    """Turn a Phrase of atoms into the best-fitting structured Expression.

    Strategy:

    * Filter out function-word atoms.
    * Scan for possessive pattern: PROPN/NOUN + possessive PART + ... + NOUN.
      The trailing NOUN becomes the head; the leading entity is the
      possessor.
    * If exactly one entity atom remains, return ``Entity(head=...)``,
      attaching any ADJ/ADV in the phrase as ``modifier`` (the
      comparison axis).
    * If no entity atoms remain but there are content atoms (e.g., a
      Phrase of only predicates), return the Phrase unchanged.
    * If multiple distinct entities remain without possessive structure,
      pick the rightmost as the head; B5 v1 doesn't model compound
      entities.
    """
    # Bound degree words are grammatical operations. Their ordinal result is
    # retained on the operand Atom; their source positions remain in the trace.
    atoms = [atom for atom in phrase.atoms if not atom.degree_modifier]
    if not atoms:
        return phrase

    # The phrase's modifier (ADJ/ADV) is the comparison axis — preserve it
    # so axis_of_comparison can recover it post-resolution.
    modifier = _first_adj_or_adv(atoms)

    # Find any possessive marker positions
    possessive_indices = [i for i, a in enumerate(atoms) if _is_possessive_marker(a)]
    if possessive_indices:
        # Take the first possessive split: everything left is the
        # possessor span; everything right (after dropping the 's) is
        # the head span.
        split_idx = possessive_indices[0]
        left = atoms[:split_idx]
        right = atoms[split_idx + 1 :]
        possessor_entity = _collapse_phrase_to_entity(Phrase(atoms=left))
        head_entity = _collapse_phrase_to_entity(Phrase(atoms=right))
        if isinstance(head_entity, Entity) and isinstance(possessor_entity, Entity):
            return Entity(
                head=head_entity.head,
                possessor=possessor_entity,
                modifier=modifier or head_entity.modifier,
            )
        if isinstance(head_entity, Entity):
            return head_entity  # possessor couldn't be resolved; drop it
        # Head couldn't be resolved either — fall through to default
        # phrase return
        return phrase

    # Coordinate NPs only when the coordinator actually follows a nominal
    # head. In "long and thick bone of the skeleton", and joins modifiers,
    # NOT bone and skeleton across the intervening preposition.
    split = next(
        (
            i
            for i, a in enumerate(atoms)
            if a.pos == "CCONJ"
            and a.lemma in _COORDINATOR_LEMMAS
            and any(_is_entity_atom(x) for x in atoms[:i])
            and not any(x.pos == "ADP" for x in atoms[:i])
            and any(_is_entity_atom(x) for x in atoms[i + 1 :])
        ),
        None,
    )
    if split is not None:
        left = _collapse_phrase_to_entity(Phrase(atoms=atoms[:split]))
        right = _collapse_phrase_to_entity(Phrase(atoms=atoms[split + 1 :]))
        members = (
            (left, *right.members)
            if isinstance(right, Coordination) and right.conjunction == atoms[split].lemma
            else (left, right)
        )
        return Coordination(members=members, conjunction=atoms[split].lemma, modifier=modifier)

    # A nominal of-postmodifier stays attached to its noun. Preserve the
    # actual relation in the existing restriction/event roleframe, rather
    # than treating its object as another argument, name part, or owner.
    of_index = next(
        (
            i
            for i, a in enumerate(atoms)
            if a.pos == "ADP"
            and a.lemma == "of"
            and any(_is_entity_atom(x) for x in atoms[:i])
            and any(_is_entity_atom(x) for x in atoms[i + 1 :])
        ),
        None,
    )
    if of_index is not None:
        head = _collapse_phrase_to_entity(Phrase(atoms=atoms[:of_index]))
        anchor = _collapse_phrase_to_entity(Phrase(atoms=atoms[of_index + 1 :]))
        bare_head = head
        while isinstance(bare_head, Op) and bare_head.operation == "REL_RESTRICT":
            bare_head = bare_head.args[0]
        relation = Op(primitive="of", operation="EVENT", arity=2, args=[bare_head, anchor])
        return Op(primitive="REL", operation="REL_RESTRICT", arity=2, args=[head, relation])

    entity_atoms = [a for a in atoms if _is_entity_atom(a)]
    # Coordinated adjective predicates modify ONE head. All conjuncts and
    # their individual degree survive in existing TYPE_ASSERT/COORD nodes;
    # Entity.modifier's single-axis compatibility field cannot store them.
    if len(entity_atoms) == 1:
        head_index = atoms.index(entity_atoms[0])
        modifiers = [a for a in atoms[:head_index] if a.pos in {"ADJ", "ADV"}]
        coordinator = next((a for a in atoms[:head_index] if a.pos == "CCONJ" and a.lemma in _COORDINATOR_LEMMAS), None)
        if coordinator is not None and len(modifiers) > 1:
            head = Entity(head=entity_atoms[0], role=entity_atoms[0].role)
            kind = Coordination(members=tuple(modifiers), conjunction=coordinator.lemma)
            restriction = Op(primitive="COPULA", operation="TYPE_ASSERT", arity=2, args=[head, kind])
            return Op(primitive="REL", operation="REL_RESTRICT", arity=2, args=[head, restriction])

    # No possessive — pick the entity head (rightmost entity atom).
    if len(entity_atoms) == 1:
        return Entity(
            head=entity_atoms[0],
            role=entity_atoms[0].role,
            modifier=modifier,
        )
    if len(entity_atoms) > 1:
        # First ask whether this is really SEVERAL noun phrases the role-blind argument
        # window swept into one slot (a ditransitive's recipient+theme, an object+adjunct,
        # an object+complement). If NP boundaries split it into >= 2 segments, return an
        # ArgSplit (the caller flattens it into separate predicate arguments) — true
        # role-split. A genuine multi-token NAME ("Lady Macbeth": consecutive PROPN, no
        # determiner boundary) does NOT split and falls through to the demi-word below.
        segments = _split_into_np_segments(atoms)
        if segments:
            members = tuple(_collapse_phrase_to_entity(Phrase(atoms=seg)) for seg in segments)
            members = tuple(m for m in members if isinstance(m, (Entity, Coordination)))
            if len(members) >= 2:
                return ArgSplit(members=members)

        # Multiple contiguous undifferentiated nominals with no coordinator, no possessive,
        # and no NP boundary — a **demi-word** ("Lady Macbeth"). The structure (one slot, no
        # coordination) says it is one unit; keep the whole span as the referent's identity
        # (rightmost as the syntactic head), so it no longer collapses to its head token and
        # unify with a bare "Macbeth".
        return Entity(
            head=entity_atoms[-1],
            role=entity_atoms[-1].role,
            modifier=modifier,
            span=tuple(a.lemma for a in entity_atoms),
        )

    # No entity atoms at all — return atoms without function words,
    # preserving the Phrase shape.
    content_atoms = [a for a in atoms if a.pos not in _FUNCTION_POS]
    if not content_atoms:
        return phrase
    if len(content_atoms) == 1:
        return content_atoms[0]
    return Phrase(atoms=content_atoms)
def _bind_pronouns(expr: Expression) -> Expression:
    """Substitute pronouns with the most-recent COMPATIBLE prior entity.

    Walks left-to-right in document order, binding each pronoun to the most-recent
    non-pronoun entity — but with two binding-theory refinements over the bare
    most-recent rule (which mis-bound a clausemate subject and collapsed two pronouns
    onto one entity):

    * **Anti-reflexive (Principle B):** a (non-reflexive) pronoun argument of a clause
      does not bind to a *co-argument* of that same clause. So "The brother betrayed
      him" → ``him`` ≠ brother (stays unresolved rather than reflexive); "...it feared
      him" → ``him`` ≠ the fearer.
    * **Distinctness:** two pronoun arguments of one clause bind to *different*
      entities, so "the wolf chased the fox and it feared him" → ``it`` = fox, ``him``
      = wolf (not both fox).

    A pronoun with no compatible antecedent is left unresolved — better than a wrong
    bind. (Cross-sentence antecedents are out of scope here: emit is per-sentence.)
    """
    seen_entities: List[Entity] = []

    def _bind_one(e: Entity, excluded: set) -> Expression:
        """Bind pronoun ``e`` to the most-recent prior non-pronoun entity whose head is
        not in ``excluded`` (its clause's co-arguments + entities already taken by a
        sibling pronoun). Returns the pronoun unchanged if none qualifies."""
        # VP-coordination shared subject: a subject-less coordinated clause ("He …and
        # murdered him") inherits the prior conjunct's subject as the *same token* (same
        # position) — a syntactic copy, not a fresh anaphor. Corefer it with that exact
        # occurrence rather than scanning past it to a nearer co-argument, which would
        # mis-bind "…and murdered him" → murder(king, …). Token identity, not a prior:
        # airtight, and it leaves genuine anaphora (recency + distinctness, e.g. "the wolf
        # chased the fox and it feared him") untouched — those pronouns have distinct
        # positions, so this never fires for them.
        for prior in reversed(seen_entities):
            if prior.head.position == e.head.position and prior.head.lemma == e.head.lemma:
                return Entity(head=prior.head, possessor=prior.possessor, role=e.role)
        for prior in reversed(seen_entities):
            if _is_pronoun_atom(prior.head):
                continue
            if prior.head.lemma in excluded:  # by referent (lemma), not atom id:
                continue  # the co-arg may recur as a distinct atom
            return Entity(head=prior.head, possessor=prior.possessor, role=e.role)
        return e

    def _walk(e: Expression) -> Expression:
        if isinstance(e, Entity):
            # Default binding (a pronoun NOT inside an EVENT's arg list — e.g. a direct
            # operand of a clause-linker): plain most-recent, no co-argument exclusion.
            if _is_pronoun_atom(e.head):
                bound = _bind_one(e, set())
                if bound is e:
                    seen_entities.append(e)  # unresolved → still a referent slot
                return bound
            seen_entities.append(e)
            return e
        if isinstance(e, Op):
            # Anti-reflexive + distinctness apply only to EVENT, whose args are genuine
            # co-arguments (agent/patient) — they cannot corefer. A clause-linking op
            # (CAUSAL_SOURCE / TEMPORAL / IMPLIES / CLAUSE_COORD) takes whole CLAUSES, so
            # a pronoun in one clause MAY bind into the sibling clause ("Mike left
            # because he was tired" → he = Mike); bind those by plain recency.
            if e.operation != "EVENT":
                return replace(e, args=[_walk(a) for a in e.args])
            new_args: List[Expression] = [None] * len(e.args)  # type: ignore[list-item]
            # Pass 1: resolve the non-pronoun args first — they are this clause's
            # co-arguments, which its pronoun args must avoid (anti-reflexive).
            excluded: set = set()
            for i, a in enumerate(e.args):
                if isinstance(a, Entity) and _is_pronoun_atom(a.head):
                    continue
                new_args[i] = _walk(a)
                if isinstance(new_args[i], Entity):
                    excluded.add(new_args[i].head.lemma)
            # Pass 2: bind pronoun args, avoiding co-arguments AND each other (distinct).
            for i, a in enumerate(e.args):
                if new_args[i] is not None:
                    continue
                bound = _bind_one(a, excluded)
                new_args[i] = bound
                if bound is a:  # unresolved → still a referent slot
                    seen_entities.append(a)
                else:  # bound: next sibling pronoun avoids it
                    excluded.add(bound.head.lemma)
            return replace(e, args=new_args)
        if isinstance(e, Negation):
            return Negation(operand=_walk(e.operand))
        if isinstance(e, Coordination):
            return replace(e, members=tuple(_walk(member) for member in e.members))
        if isinstance(e, Phrase):
            return Phrase(atoms=list(e.atoms))
        return e

    return _walk(expr)
def _refine(expr: Expression) -> Expression:
    """Inner walker — collapse Phrases into Entities, leave other nodes."""
    if isinstance(expr, Phrase):
        # May return an ArgSplit (a multi-NP slot) — the Op branch below consumes it; a
        # bare top-level Phrase that splits is collapsed to its primary in `resolve`.
        return _collapse_phrase_to_entity(expr)
    if isinstance(expr, Op):
        # Refine each arg; an ArgSplit (one slot that held several NPs) flattens into
        # SEPARATE args for a variadic EVENT (the role-split — recipient+theme become
        # distinct arguments), but for a fixed-arity operator only its primary member is
        # kept so the operator's arity is preserved.
        new_args: List[Expression] = []
        is_event = expr.operation == "EVENT"
        for a in expr.args:
            r = _refine(a)
            if isinstance(r, ArgSplit):
                if is_event:
                    new_args.extend(r.members)
                else:
                    new_args.append(r.members[0])
            else:
                new_args.append(r)
        return replace(expr, arity=len(new_args), args=new_args)
    if isinstance(expr, Negation):
        return Negation(operand=_refine(expr.operand))
    if isinstance(expr, Atom):
        # Lone atoms — if entity-bearing, wrap as Entity
        if _is_entity_atom(expr):
            return Entity(head=expr, role=expr.role)
        return expr
    return expr

### GSE/symbolic/predicates.py
class Event:
    """A verb roleframe — the base-case predicate for a plain clause.

    "Duncan rewarded Macbeth" → ``Event(verb="reward", agent=duncan,
    patient=macbeth)``; "Rex barks" → ``Event(verb="bark", agent=rex)``. This is
    the predicate the operator set was missing: a clause with an ordinary
    transitive/intransitive verb and no comparison/type/causation operator. It
    maps 1:1 to Genesis's ``makeRoleFrame(subject, verb, object)`` — and, crucially,
    it is what lets a *sub*-clause survive as structure instead of collapsing to
    its salient entity (the cause/effect of a Causation, the inner act of a
    Control are Events, not bare nouns).

    Args:
        verb: the clause's verb lemma (the relation).
        agent: the subject filler.
        patient: the object/complement filler, or ``None`` for an intransitive.
        themes: the SECONDARY arguments a ditransitive / object+complement split off
            ("gave Lady Macbeth a letter" → patient=Lady Macbeth, themes=(letter,)). Empty
            for an ordinary clause. They are PRESERVED but NOT promoted into the default
            analysis — a latent "theme-curious" surface, revivable, that keeps the clean
            primary read the viz wants while never destroying the dropped constituents.
        modal: the modal primes of the clause's auxiliaries ("He might leave" → ``("MAYBE",)``); empty for a plain
            clause. A modal event is stated as possible or necessary, never as a fact
            (:func:`GSE.symbolic.modality.modal_force`, #66).
    """

    verb: str
    agent: Operand
    patient: Optional[Operand] = None
    themes: tuple = ()
    modal: tuple = ()
    duration: Duration | None = None

def _native_example_support(self, position, lemma, senses, pos):
        """Make attested non-nominal identities reachable without a POS override.

        Compare the complete sentence construction rather than isolated cue
        words. This deliberately abstains on underspecified or novel uses;
        grammatical role alone, frequency and already-filled banks cannot
        license a definition. Existing nominal type-thread grounding is kept
        separate because noun and verb threads are not comparable types.
        """
        start, end = self._bounds(position, self.sentence_boundaries)
        actual = tuple((t.lemma_.casefold(), t.pos_) for t in self.doc[start + 1 : end])
        witnesses = {}
        for entry_id, sense in senses.items():
            examples = [
                example for example in sense.examples if _native_example_signature(example, lemma, pos) == actual
            ]
            if examples:
                witnesses[entry_id] = {
                    "witness_kind": "WORDNET_NATIVE_EXAMPLE_CONSTRUCTION",
                    "native_synset": sense.synset,
                    "native_examples": examples,
                    "construction_signature": [list(pair) for pair in actual],
                    "eligible_pos": pos,
                    "source_record_id": entry_id,
                }
        return _unique_native_witness(witnesses)
def _construction_support(self, position, lemma, senses, *, definition_only=False):
        """Bind multiple gloss cues or an exact derivation in a linked clause."""
        tokens, linked = self._construction_span(position)
        cues = {
            token.lemma_: token.pos_
            for token in tokens
            if token.i != position
            and token.lemma_ != lemma
            and token.pos_ in _CONTENT_POS
            and token.lemma_ not in _GENERIC_TERMS
            and not token.is_stop
            and not is_numeral(token.lemma_)
        }
        type_witness = self._construction_type(position, tokens, linked)
        predication = self._definition_predication(position)
        sentence_start, sentence_end = self._bounds(position, self.sentence_boundaries)
        # A construction span can stop at a coordinator. The material before
        # an alternative is not, by itself, asserted context: deriving a noun
        # identity from just that first disjunct would silently discard the
        # other reading. Complete definition matching already checks this
        # scope; weaker gloss/derivation evidence must not bypass that check.
        alternative_context = any(t.lemma_ == "or" for t in self.doc[sentence_start + 1 : sentence_end])
        derivations = {word: _verb_derivations(word) for word, pos in cues.items() if pos == "VERB"}
        linked_verbs = {t.lemma_ for t in tokens if linked is not None and t.i > linked and t.pos_ == "VERB"}
        witnesses, definition_witnesses = {}, {}
        for entry_id, sense in senses.items():
            gloss = dict(_gloss_content(sense.gloss))
            matched = frozenset(gloss.keys() & cues.keys())
            exact, related = self._derivation_support(sense, gloss, matched, derivations, linked_verbs, type_witness)
            verb_match = any(gloss[word] == cues[word] == "VERB" for word in matched)
            typed = self._matches_construction_type(sense, type_witness, matched, gloss)
            repeated = self._matches_definition_predication(sense, predication)
            if repeated or (
                not definition_only
                and not alternative_context
                and (exact or (verb_match and len(matched) >= 2) or related or typed)
            ):
                witnesses[entry_id] = {
                    "gloss_terms": sorted(matched),
                    "exact_derivation": exact,
                    "related_derivation": related,
                    "construction_type": predication if repeated else type_witness if typed or related else None,
                }
                if repeated:
                    definition_witnesses[entry_id] = witnesses[entry_id]
        # Complete definition identity precedes weaker derivational similarity;
        # two exact definitions still abstain rather than choosing by order.
        result = _unique_native_witness(definition_witnesses or witnesses)
        if alternative_context:
            result["unasserted_context"] = "DISJUNCTIVE_CONSTRUCTION_ALTERNATIVES"
        return result

### GSE/api/encoder.py
def encode(self, text: str) -> OperationTrace:
        """
        Encode text to HDC vector with full operation trace.

        Args:
            text: Input text (sentence)

        Returns:
            OperationTrace with all encoding steps
        """
        from GSE.nlp.morphology import negation_admission, negation_evidence

        # 1. Tokenize
        doc = self.nlp(text)
        head_position = next((i for i, token in enumerate(doc) if token.pos_ != "PUNCT"), None)
        lexical_rows: Dict[str, Dict] = {}
        grammatical_rows: Dict[Tuple[str, str, str], Optional[Tuple[str, str, Dict]]] = {}

        # 1b. Upstream parse repair: spaCy mistags some verbs as nouns
        #     ("Macbeth murders Duncan"). Promote buried verbs to POS=VERB so the
        #     position-based EVENT synthesis downstream finds a predicate.
        promote_to_verb = verbs_to_promote(doc)

        # 1c. Clause-coordinating "and"/"or": a coordinator with a predicate on
        #     BOTH sides joins two CLAUSES (WS1 — derived from the verb-inventory,
        #     no spaCy arcs), distinct from NP/VP coordination. Marked as the
        #     clause-linking CLAUSE_COORD operator so it becomes a clause boundary.
        clause_coords = self._clause_coordinator_positions(doc, promote_to_verb)
        clause_coords |= self._copula_clause_coordinator_positions(doc)

        # 1c'. Fronted conditional "if": a clause-initial "if" with a predicate in
        #      its antecedent → the IMPLIES clause-linker. Not a lexicon operator
        #      ("if" carries no comp_operation), so it is marked here like "and".
        implies_positions = self._conditional_positions(doc, promote_to_verb)

        # 1c''. Fronted temporal subordinator "when/while/after/before": a clause-initial
        #       one with a predicate in its subordinate clause → the TEMPORAL clause-linker
        #       (both clauses asserted). Like "if", carries no lexicon comp_operation.
        temporal_positions = self._temporal_positions(doc, promote_to_verb)

        # 1d. Arc-free core syntactic roles (positional), computed once for the
        #     sentence. ``None`` falls the per-token extractor back to spaCy dep_.
        syn_map = self._syn_roles(doc, promote_to_verb) if self._arcfree_syn else None
        # 1d'. Parse-strand auto-repair: on a DEGRADED clause the native Tier-1 repair
        #      re-assigns roles (commit only) before EVENT synthesis; clean parses pass
        #      through untouched. Guarded so a repair failure never breaks encode.
        if syn_map is not None and not getattr(self, "_in_repair", False):
            try:
                self._in_repair = True
                syn_map = self._parse_repair().repair_syn_map(doc, syn_map)
            except Exception:
                pass
            finally:
                self._in_repair = False

        # 2. Process each token
        from GSE.symbolic.lexical_grounding import LexicalGrounding

        grounding = (
            LexicalGrounding(self.conn, doc, clause_coords | implies_positions | temporal_positions)
            if self._definition_database
            else None
        )
        token_traces: List[TokenTrace] = []
        token_vectors: List[Tuple[int, SparseVector, CompositionalMetadata]] = []
        operator_indices: List[int] = []
        comp_meta: CompositionalMetadata

        for i, tok in enumerate(doc):
            # Lexicon lookup (static primitives from database)
            lemma = tok.lemma_.lower()
            lookup_form = lemma
            grammatical = None
            contextual_pos = None
            if self._definition_database:
                # Predicate promotion assigns a sentence role; an existing AUX
                # reading still licenses its exact grammatical definition.
                grammar_key = (tok.text.lower(), lemma, tok.pos_)
                if grammar_key not in grammatical_rows:
                    grammatical_rows[grammar_key] = self._grammatical_definition(*grammar_key)
                grammatical = grammatical_rows[grammar_key]
            if self._definition_database and grammatical is None and tok.text.lower() != lemma:
                if lemma not in lexical_rows:
                    lexical_rows[lemma] = self.lexical_lookup(lemma)
                # Exact surface spelling can recover a missing lemma (tired ->
                # tire), but never resolves an ambiguous lemma by substitution.
                if lexical_rows[lemma].get("selection_status") == "NOT_FOUND":
                    lookup_form = tok.text.lower()
            lexical: Dict[str, Any]
            if grammatical is not None:
                lookup_form, entry_id, lexical = grammatical
                if grounding is None:
                    raise ValueError("GRAMMATICAL_SELECTION_REQUIRES_GROUNDING")
                eligibility = grounding.grammatical_eligibility(i, lookup_form, entry_id)
                if eligibility["code"] == "CONTEXTUAL_DEFINITION_SELECTED":
                    entry_id = eligibility["entry_id"]
                    lexical = {
                        **self.lexical_lookup(lookup_form, entry_id=entry_id),
                        "reading_eligibility": eligibility,
                        "contextual_grounding": eligibility["contextual_grounding"],
                    }
                    # An exact source/role witness repairs this occurrence,
                    # not every occurrence sharing the parser's POS/spelling.
                    contextual_pos = "NOUN"
                elif eligibility["code"] == "GRAMMATICAL_CONTEXT_CONFLICT":
                    # POS is evidence, not a veto over native/context facts.
                    # Retain both rivals, but publish neither reading nor banks.
                    lexical = {
                        **lexical,
                        "state": "unread",
                        "reason": eligibility["code"],
                        "selection_status": "CONFLICT",
                        "selected_record": None,
                        "sense_resolved": False,
                        "primitives": {},
                        "domains": {},
                        "hierarchy": {},
                        "primitive_evidence": [],
                        "reading_eligibility": eligibility,
                    }
                    entry_id = None
                else:
                    lexical = {**lexical, "reading_eligibility": eligibility}
                word_prims, sent_prims, comp_meta = self._lookup_lexeme(
                    lookup_form, entry_id=entry_id, lexical_evidence=lexical
                )
            else:
                if lookup_form not in lexical_rows:
                    lexical_rows[lookup_form] = self.lexical_lookup(lookup_form)
                lexical = lexical_rows[lookup_form]
                entry_id = None
                if (
                    grounding is not None
                    and (tok.pos_ in {"NOUN", "PROPN", "VERB", "ADJ", "ADV"} or i in promote_to_verb)
                    and lexical.get("selection_status") == "AMBIGUOUS"
                ):
                    alternatives = lexical["candidate_entry_ids"]
                    eligible_pos = "VERB" if i in promote_to_verb else "NOUN" if tok.pos_ == "PROPN" else tok.pos_
                    selection = grounding.select(i, lookup_form, alternatives, pos=eligible_pos)
                    if selection["code"] in {"EXACT_WORDNET_SENSE", "PRIMARY_UNIT_FRAME"}:
                        entry_id = selection["entry_id"]
                        lexical = self.lexical_lookup(lookup_form, entry_id=entry_id)
                    lexical = {**lexical, "contextual_grounding": {**selection, "considered_entry_ids": alternatives}}
                # The trace and vector must consume the same selected source row.
                word_prims, sent_prims, comp_meta = self._lookup_lexeme(
                    lookup_form, entry_id=entry_id, lexical_evidence=lexical
                )
            if self._definition_database:
                lexical = {**lexical, "lookup_form": lookup_form, "parser_lemma": lemma}
            negative = negation_evidence(lemma)

            # Recognition does not authorize overriding a different selected
            # lexical sense. Admit only a supported, compatible signed base.
            if negative.get("feature") == NEGATION:
                base_lemma = negative["base"]
                if base_lemma not in lexical_rows:
                    lexical_rows[base_lemma] = self.lexical_lookup(base_lemma)
                admission: Dict[str, Any] = negation_admission(
                    negative, lexical, lexical_rows[base_lemma], "VERB" if i in promote_to_verb else tok.pos_
                )
                if self._definition_database and admission["decision"] == "compose":
                    selected = lexical.get("selected_record") or {}
                    known = selected.get("assignments", {})
                    candidate = admission["primitives"]
                    if any(candidate.get(bank, 0) != value for bank, value in known.items()):
                        admission.update(
                            decision="preserve", code="selected_definition_assignment_conflict", primitives=None
                        )
                    elif selected and any(
                        value not in selected["domains"].get(bank, []) for bank, value in candidate.items()
                    ):
                        admission.update(
                            decision="preserve", code="selected_definition_domain_conflict", primitives=None
                        )
                negative = {**negative, "admission": admission}
                if admission["decision"] == "compose":
                    word_prims = admission["primitives"]

            if i in clause_coords:
                comp_meta = {"comp_primitive": "COMP_AND", "comp_operation": "CLAUSE_COORD", "comp_arity": 2}
            if i in implies_positions:
                comp_meta = {"comp_primitive": "COMP_IF", "comp_operation": "IMPLIES", "comp_arity": 2}
            if i in temporal_positions:
                comp_meta = {"comp_primitive": "COMP_WHEN", "comp_operation": "TEMPORAL", "comp_arity": 2}
            head_operation = head_linker_operation(lemma, i == head_position)
            if head_operation != "none":
                primitive = {
                    "CONTRAST": "COMP_BUT",
                    "CONSEQUENCE": "COMP_SO",
                    "CLAUSE_COORD": "COMP_AND",
                    "TEMPORAL": "COMP_WHEN",
                }[head_operation]
                comp_meta = {"comp_primitive": primitive, "comp_operation": head_operation, "comp_arity": 2}

            # DYNAMIC: Replace core syntactic role primitives based on dependency parsing
            # This ensures argument order matters (dog as SUBJ vs dog as OBJ)
            # The dynamic primitives OVERRIDE static ones for core roles
            dynamic_sent_prims = self._extract_dynamic_primitives(tok, syn_map)

            # Remove static core role primitives - dynamic parsing is authoritative
            core_roles = {"SYN_SUBJ", "SYN_OBJ", "SYN_PRED", "SYN_COMPL"}
            sent_prims = {k: v for k, v in sent_prims.items() if k not in core_roles}
            sent_prims = {**sent_prims, **dynamic_sent_prims}

            # Encode vectors
            word_vec = (
                self._encode_definition_primitives(word_prims, lexical.get("hierarchy", {}))
                if self._definition_database
                else self._encode_word_primitives(word_prims)
            )
            sent_vec = self._encode_sent_primitives(sent_prims)

            # Compose: word_full = bundle([word_vec, sent_vec])
            # Using bundle() instead of bind() to preserve both signals
            # (bind() destroys signal when word-scale and sent-scale are orthogonal)
            if word_vec.nnz > 0 and sent_vec.nnz > 0:
                full_vec = bundle([word_vec, sent_vec])
            elif word_vec.nnz > 0:
                full_vec = word_vec
            elif sent_vec.nnz > 0:
                full_vec = sent_vec
            else:
                full_vec = SparseVector.zeros(self.word_basis.dimension)

            # Create token trace
            is_operator = bool(comp_meta.get("comp_primitive"))
            token_trace = TokenTrace(
                token=tok.text,
                lemma=tok.lemma_.lower(),
                pos=(contextual_pos or ("VERB" if i in promote_to_verb else tok.pos_)),
                position=i,
                word_primitives=word_prims,
                sent_primitives=sent_prims,
                word_vec_nnz=word_vec.nnz,
                sent_vec_nnz=sent_vec.nnz,
                full_vec_nnz=full_vec.nnz,
                is_operator=is_operator,
                comp_primitive=comp_meta.get("comp_primitive"),
                comp_operation=comp_meta.get("comp_operation"),
                comp_arity=comp_meta.get("comp_arity", 0),
                lexicon_status={"primes": "found", "no_primes": "found", "no_row": "unknown", "unread": "unread"}[
                    lexical["state"]
                ],
                lexical_evidence=lexical,
                negation_evidence=negative,
                operator_tier=(
                    "discourse"
                    if head_operation != "none"
                    else "clause"
                    if is_operator
                    and (is_clause_linking(comp_meta.get("comp_operation") or "") or comp_meta.get("comp_arity") == 1)
                    else "phrase"
                )
                if is_operator
                else None,
            )
            token_traces.append(token_trace)
            token_vectors.append((i, full_vec, comp_meta))

            if is_operator:
                operator_indices.append(i)

        # Sentence degree is grammatical evidence even when lexical senses
        # abstain. It never creates a base or selects a candidate definition.
        from GSE.symbolic.expression import bind_degree_modifiers

        bind_degree_modifiers(token_traces)
        for token in token_traces:
            if not token.degree and not token.degree_modifier:
                continue
            primitives = token.word_primitives
            if token.degree_modifier and not self._definition_database:
                primitives = {}
                token.word_primitives = primitives
            hierarchy = dict(token.lexical_evidence.get("hierarchy", {}))
            bases = [bank for bank, value in primitives.items() if bank in BIPOLAR_PRIMITIVES and value]
            if token.degree and len(bases) == 1:
                target = bases[0]
                if self._definition_database:
                    hierarchy[target] = hierarchy.get(target, 0) + token.degree["level"]
                else:
                    level = primitives.get("HIER_PLUS", 0) - primitives.get("HIER_MINUS", 0) + token.degree["level"]
                    primitives = {
                        key: value for key, value in primitives.items() if key not in {"HIER_PLUS", "HIER_MINUS"}
                    }
                    if level:
                        primitives["HIER_PLUS" if level > 0 else "HIER_MINUS"] = abs(level)
                    token.word_primitives = primitives
            word_vec = (
                self._encode_definition_primitives(primitives, hierarchy)
                if self._definition_database
                else self._encode_word_primitives(primitives)
            )
            sent_vec = self._encode_sent_primitives(token.sent_primitives)
            components = [vector for vector in (word_vec, sent_vec) if vector.nnz]
            full_vec = bundle(components) if components else SparseVector.zeros(self.word_basis.dimension)
            token.word_vec_nnz = word_vec.nnz
            token.sent_vec_nnz = sent_vec.nnz
            token.full_vec_nnz = full_vec.nnz
            position, _, metadata = token_vectors[token.position]
            token_vectors[token.position] = (position, full_vec, metadata)

        # 3. Plan clauses (sequential because/so splits + embedded relative
        #    clauses), then resolve operators within their innermost clause.
        n_tokens = len(token_vectors)
        op_meta = [(op_idx, token_vectors[op_idx][2].get("comp_operation")) for op_idx in operator_indices]
        sequential = self._segment_clauses(token_traces, op_meta)
        embedded = self._detect_embedded_clauses(doc, promote_to_verb)

        # An embedded clause forces clause planning even without a sequential
        # boundary: synthesize a single implicit main clause to hang it on.
        if embedded and not sequential:
            sequential = [(0, 0, n_tokens)]

        # Unify into planned spans: (clause_id, start, end, kind, parent_id,
        # attaches_to). Sequential clauses keep ids [0..k); embedded follow.
        planned: List[Tuple[int, int, int, str, Optional[int], Optional[int]]] = [
            (cid, s, e, "sequential", None, None) for cid, s, e in sequential
        ]
        next_id = len(sequential)
        gap_roles: Dict[int, Optional[str]] = {}  # clause_id → relativizer gap role
        for s, e, kind, attaches, gap_role in embedded:
            parent = next(
                (cid for cid, ps, pe, k, _, _ in planned if k == "sequential" and ps <= attaches < pe),
                0,
            )
            # An embedded clause must not CROSS a sequential (clause-linking)
            # boundary: spaCy sometimes spans an xcomp/relcl across a coordination
            # or because/so split (e.g. it reads "Duncan and Macduff killed Macbeth"
            # as an xcomp of "murdered"). If start and end-1 fall in different
            # sequential clauses, drop the bogus embedding — the clause-linker owns it.
            seq_start = next((cid for cid, ps, pe, k, _, _ in planned if k == "sequential" and ps <= s < pe), None)
            seq_end = next((cid for cid, ps, pe, k, _, _ in planned if k == "sequential" and ps <= e - 1 < pe), None)
            if seq_start is not None and seq_start != seq_end:
                continue
            # A complement whose clause sits in a *different* sequential clause
            # than its matrix verb is really a so/because-linked clause (spaCy
            # tags the consequence verb as ccomp); the clause-linker owns it.
            if kind == "complement":
                span_clause = next(
                    (cid for cid, ps, pe, k, _, _ in planned if k == "sequential" and ps <= s < pe),
                    parent,
                )
                if span_clause != parent:
                    continue
            planned.append((next_id, s, e, kind, parent, attaches))
            gap_roles[next_id] = gap_role
            next_id += 1

        def _innermost_of(pos: int) -> Optional[tuple]:
            """Smallest planned span containing pos (embedded beats parent)."""
            best = None
            for span in planned:
                _, s, e, _, _, _ = span
                if s <= pos < e and (best is None or (e - s) < (best[2] - best[1])):
                    best = span
            return best

        def _sequential_of(pos: int) -> Optional[Tuple[int, int, int]]:
            for cid, s, e in sequential:
                if s <= pos < e:
                    return (cid, s, e)
            return None

        # Token positions inside any embedded clause — kept out of a parent
        # operator's arguments (but an operator inside the embedded clause keeps
        # its own tokens).
        embedded_tokens_by_clause: Dict[int, set] = {
            cid: set(range(s, e)) for cid, s, e, k, _, _ in planned if k != "sequential"
        }
        all_embedded_tokens = set().union(*embedded_tokens_by_clause.values()) if embedded_tokens_by_clause else set()

        operator_traces: List[OperatorTrace] = []
        operator_results: List[SparseVector] = []
        op_trace_index: Dict[int, int] = {}  # op_idx → index in operator_traces
        op_clause: Dict[int, int] = {}  # op_idx → innermost clause_id

        for op_idx in operator_indices:
            _, _, comp_meta = token_vectors[op_idx]
            operation = comp_meta.get("comp_operation")
            arg1_range: Optional[Tuple[int, int]] = None
            arg2_range: Optional[Tuple[int, int]] = None

            linking = (
                operation
                and is_clause_linking(operation)
                and head_linker_operation(token_traces[op_idx].lemma, op_idx == head_position) == "none"
            )
            if planned and linking:
                # Operands are the sequential clauses left/right of the
                # connective — whole clauses, not raw token spans.
                left = _sequential_of(op_idx - 1)
                right = _sequential_of(op_idx + 1)
                if left:
                    arg1_range = (left[1], left[2])
                if right:
                    arg2_range = (right[1], right[2])
            this_clause_id: Optional[int] = None
            if planned:
                inner = _innermost_of(op_idx)
                if inner:
                    this_clause_id = inner[0]
            if planned and not linking:
                # Within-clause operator: restrict args to its innermost clause
                # (so a THAN inside a relative clause stays inside it).
                c = _innermost_of(op_idx)
                if c:
                    op_clause[op_idx] = c[0]
                    arg1_range = (c[1], op_idx)
                    arg2_range = (op_idx + 1, c[2])

            # Keep embedded-clause tokens out of this operator's args, except
            # the operator's own embedded clause.
            excluded = set(all_embedded_tokens)
            if this_clause_id in embedded_tokens_by_clause:
                excluded -= embedded_tokens_by_clause[this_clause_id]

            op_trace, result_vec = self._resolve_operator(
                op_idx,
                comp_meta,
                token_vectors,
                token_traces,
                arg1_range,
                arg2_range,
                excluded,
            )
            if op_trace:
                op_trace_index[op_idx] = len(operator_traces)
                operator_traces.append(op_trace)
                if result_vec and result_vec.nnz > 0:
                    operator_results.append(result_vec)

        # Build the clause spans for the trace (only when actually planned).
        clauses: List[ClauseSpan] = []
        for cid, s, e, kind, parent_id, attaches in planned:
            within = [
                op_trace_index[oi] for oi in operator_indices if oi in op_trace_index and op_clause.get(oi) == cid
            ]
            clauses.append(
                ClauseSpan(
                    clause_id=cid,
                    token_start=s,
                    token_end=e,
                    operator_indices=within,
                    kind=kind,
                    parent_id=parent_id,
                    attaches_to_token=attaches,
                    gap_role=gap_roles.get(cid),
                )
            )

        # 4. Position encoding + bundling
        components: List[SparseVector] = []

        for i, (pos, full_vec, _) in enumerate(token_vectors):
            if full_vec.nnz > 0:
                # Apply positional permutation
                positioned = permute(full_vec, shift=pos * 100)
                components.append(positioned)

        # Add operator results
        components.extend(operator_results)

        # Bundle all components
        if components:
            sentence_vec = bundle(components)
        else:
            sentence_vec = SparseVector.zeros(self.word_basis.dimension)

        # 5. Compute primitive activations
        word_activations = self._compute_primitive_activations(sentence_vec, self.word_basis)
        sent_activations = self._compute_primitive_activations(sentence_vec, self.sent_basis)

        # 6. Compute vector hash
        vector_hash = self._hash_vector(sentence_vec)

        # 7. Create trace
        trace = OperationTrace(
            input_text=text,
            tokens=token_traces,
            operators=operator_traces,
            final_nnz=sentence_vec.nnz,
            sparsity=sentence_vec.sparsity,
            word_primitive_activations=word_activations,
            sent_primitive_activations=sent_activations,
            vector_hash=vector_hash,
            clauses=clauses,
        )
        trace.vector = sentence_vec

        return trace
